Spike confirmed: api/mcp-spike.ts implements MCP Streamable HTTP with one
hardcoded tool (get-example-set) using @modelcontextprotocol/sdk's
StreamableHTTPServerTransport in stateless mode (sessionIdGenerator:
undefined) — the SDK's own documented pattern for serverless deployments.

What worked:
- End-to-end verified locally with the SDK's real client transport
  (StreamableHTTPClientTransport) driving the actual handler wrapped in a
  plain Node http server that mimics Vercel's contract (JSON body
  pre-parsed onto req.body): initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call all
  round-tripped correctly. GET/DELETE correctly 405 since stateless mode
  has no session to resume/terminate.
- Stateless mode (new McpServer + transport constructed per request, no
  in-memory session map) fits Vercel's per-invocation isolation model
  cleanly — no code needed to survive across calls.
- api/mcp-spike.ts sits outside tsconfig's "include": ["src"] and outside
  the Vite build, so it's inert w.r.t. `npm run typecheck`/`npm run
  build`/tests (all still pass) and safe to delete or repurpose wholesale
  before Task 1.

Transport quirks / open questions for Task 1:
- Session state (auth, per-conversation memory) can't live in an in-memory
  map the way many MCP server examples do — cold starts / multi-instance
  means each request may hit a different process. Any real session state
  needs external storage (KV/DB), or lean fully stateless per-request like
  this spike.
- vercel.json has a SPA catch-all rewrite ("/(.*)" -> "/index.html").
  Vercel is documented to check filesystem/API routes before applying
  rewrites, so /api/* should take precedence, but this wasn't confirmed
  against a real deploy (see below) and is worth double-checking early in
  Task 1.
- NOT verified: actual behavior on Vercel's hosted infra (cold start
  latency, function timeout limits, whether a real MCP client like Claude
  Desktop/Code connects through Vercel's edge/proxy without issue). This
  sandbox has no Vercel CLI/project link or credentials, so only local
  verification (against the real handler code) was possible. Recommend
  Task 1 push a preview deploy early and re-run the same
  initialize/list/call check against the live URL before building out real
  tools.
